notes: Cats: Champagne in each bank carries the whole subject, the method, the districts, the crus, the label codes and the service; the Champagne stems under Producers & Icons, History & Figures, Food & Pairing and Sparkling Wine World are left out because those categories range far wider. Chapters: the Régionale chapter champagne and the Village chapter Champagne. Regions: the champagne article, whose places run the districts with their Grand Cru villages and whose producers hold the Court's six houses and four growers. Country: france for the climate card and the Crémant card that sets Champagne apart. Grapes: the two of the Court's three that carry a profile; Meunier has none. Techniques: the traditional method for the Court's Winemaking cells, assemblage for the blend of villages, grapes and reserve years, rosé methods for the rosé by blending the Style row names. Service tables: sparkling, the opening step by step, which is the Court's Certified service cell; temperatures (Champagne at 8 to 10 C) and glassware (flute and tulip) for the rest of the service.
